transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Ortega (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Sunrise - Head of Infra), Maya Sanchez (Sunrise CTO), Evan Lee (Sunrise Procurement)

Summary: quick renewal check-in + scope expansion: Sunrise is evaluating a Q3 capacity upgrade (approx. 3x current reserved GPUs), wants to add EU region, and is considering a 12-month contract extension with committed Dedicated capacity. Security/compliance are ok (SOC2 in place) but want KMS/HSM details and SSO/SAML flow. Agreed next steps: pricing spreadsheet, perf notes, contract amendment draft, and traffic forecast.

Transcript:
[00:00] Laura: hey everybody, thanks for jumping on, how's it going?
[00:05] Ravi: good thanks, good to see you. we wanted to run through the renewal + expansion asks — Q3 capacity and EU region primarily.
[00:12] Laura: great, yep, quick agenda: pricing/commit, region availability, perf/benchmarks, security touch points, next steps. Miguel is with me for the perf stuff.
[00:20] Miguel: hi all, yeah i'll cover the Dedicated sizing and some bench numbers we ran last week.
[00:25] Maya: quick context — our current deployment is 4x reserved gpus in us-west, running inference for payments risk scoring and receipt parsing; average p95 latency is around 220ms but during peak promo windows we're seeing increased queues. We want to move to a larger reserved pool and add EU to serve a new merchant group.
[00:44] Miguel: okay, that makes sense. are you looking strictly at more raw GPU count or also multi-region redundancy?
[00:50] Ravi: both. primary need is capacity in us-west for Q3 (roughly 3x current peak — so planning for 12 GPUs reserved), plus EU-west for about 4 GPUs initially.
[01:02] Laura: cool. on pricing we usually show two options — increased reserved capacity commit (monthly commit with discounts) vs. burst/buffer add-on for seasonal spikes. for a 12-month commit we can improve unit pricing ~18-22% depending on the exact RU.
[01:20] Evan: when you say RU — you mean reserved units / GPUs — clarify the billing model so procurement can size it.
[01:26] Laura: yes, reserved GPU equivalent. i'll send a spreadsheet that maps GPUs to committed RU, expected throughput, and estimated monthly bill. that'll show per-token and per-hour numbers so you can compare to current spend.
[01:36] Miguel: quick perf note — in our latest tests on Redwood Dedicated, the model (open-llm variant you use) with quantization and continuous batching gave us ~15% cost improvement vs default and p95 latencies around 160-180ms on A100-equivalent configs. on multi-node bursts, KV cache warms up and improves tail latency — but warm start behavior depends on session stickiness.
[02:02] Maya: couple questions: 1) do you support EU data residency for logs and telemetry? 2) how does KMS integrate for keys — we have a managed HSM and need to ensure keys never leave our KMS.
[02:15] Miguel: yes, for Redwood Private/Dedicated we can pin region for logs and optionally ship audit logs to your S3 in eu-west. KMS — we integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM, and you can bring keys; we use envelope encryption so keys are never stored in plaintext in the control plane. i will send the KMS integration note — there's some ops steps.
[02:33] Ravi: that's good. any SOC2 or ISO certs we should reference?
[02:37] Laura: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II; i'll attach the compliance pack. also for SSO we support SAML / OIDC and RBAC for team-level controls.
[02:46] Evan: procurement wants the contract amendment draft early — if we commit to 12 months and add eu region, we need pricing + SLA language. what's typical SLA for Dedicated?
[02:56] Laura: Dedicated is SLA-backed; uptime targets that we can include in the amendment — i'll flag the standard 99.9 uptime for reserved pools and include latency SLOs as guidance. for enterprise we do premium SLA add-ons if needed.
[03:10] Miguel: one more perf nuance — depending on your traffic distribution, we may recommend different instance sizes in EU vs US. for example, heavy short-lived chat-like requests are better with smaller instances and more autoscale headroom; long-form batching benefits from larger GPU instances with more memory. i'll put suggested configs in the perf doc.
[03:30] Maya: our main workloads: (1) risk scoring — short requests, high qps; (2) invoice/receipt OCR postprocessing — longer sequences but lower qps. sounds like mixed pattern.
[03:40] Miguel: exactly — so for risk scoring we'll optimize for latency with smaller instances + continuous batching + prefix caching. for OCR we'll use larger instances with KV cache tuning.
[03:50] Ravi: how does prefix/KV cache work across regions? if a user hits EU for risk scoring, and their profile is in US, do we have cross-region cache implications?
[03:59] Miguel: good question — cache is per serving pool/region. we recommend routing customers to regional variants to avoid cross-region cache misses; smart routing can help preserve latency. there are tradeoffs — cross-region fallback is possible but will increase tail latency.
[04:15] Evan: about cost: if we add EU region, will that change pricing materially? regional price differentials?
[04:22] Laura: slight regional premium sometimes applies due to infra costs; i'll show region-adjusted numbers in the pricing sheet. overall committed discount applies across your entire reserved commitment if you commit globally.
[04:32] Maya: security/enterprise: we need to see audit logs retention options and proof of encryption in transit + at rest.
[04:38] Laura: yes — we have configurable retention and can route logs to your S3 or our secure log storage with retention policy. encryption in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3 — at rest we use envelope encryption and you can bring your KMS. I'll include the security doc.
[04:50] Ravi: any downtime or maintenance windows that would affect throughput? we run promos at midnight PST sometimes.
[04:56] Miguel: maintenance is scheduled and we can provide blackout windows — for Dedicated reserved pools, maintenance is low and we provide canary nodes + automatic failover. we'll include the maintenance policy.
[05:06] Maya: performance baseline — you said p95 160-180ms for that config; on our current stack p95 is 220ms. if we moved to 12 GPUs and enable the batching/caching configs, what realistic p95 improvement should we expect?
[05:18] Miguel: conservatively 20-30% p95 improvement for the risk scoring pattern given more headroom and optimized kernels; for OCR, latency might stay similar but throughput increases.
[05:30] Ravi: ok, that's promising. one last procurement item — do you support PO + invoice or do you need a contract first?
[05:37] Laura: we can do either — for initial renewal we usually do contract amendment + PO. Evan, we'll work with legal to get you the amendment draft.
[05:44] Evan: timeline wise, we want to lock pricing by mid-May to hit Q3 provisioning.
[05:50] Laura: understood — so our timeline: Laura sends pricing & region sheet (May 8), Miguel sends perf notes + instance recs (May 11), Sunrise provides traffic forecast (May 14), Evan & Laura review contract amendment (May 12). anything else?
[06:05] Maya: can Miguel share a short sample benchmark run we can replicate? we'd like to validate on our side for a single model.
[06:12] Miguel: yes, i'll attach a lightweight benchmark script and a checklist. you can run it against a short-lived Dedicated test cluster or we can run it in our sandbox for you.
[06:22] Ravi: sandbox run would be helpful; if you can pre-provision an EU test node that mirrors the proposed config that would speed validation.
[06:30] Miguel: we can do that — it'll take a couple days to provision; i'll note the region and instance type.
[06:36] Laura: good — procurement and legal items aside, any blockers on your side?
[06:41] Evan: just legal standard terms; also need clarity on data residency and subprocessor list which legal will request.
[06:48] Laura: i'll attach the subprocessor list and compliance pack.
[06:52] Maya: on routing — is there support for sticky sessions or IP affinity to preserve KV cache?
[06:56] Miguel: yes we have session affinity options; sticky sessions help KV cache wins. we'll show recommended routing policy.
[07:04] Ravi: okay, sounds good.
[07:06] Laura: quick recap and next steps — pricing sheet to Evan and Ravi by Friday (May 8), Miguel's perf doc + bench by May 11, contract amendment draft by May 12, traffic forecast by May 14. we'll also schedule a follow-up stand-up next week if needed.
[07:22] Evan: thanks everyone.
[07:24] Maya: thanks.
[45:00] End of meeting.

Notes/Attachments referenced: "Pricing matrix (to be sent)", "Redwood Dedicated perf notes (to be sent)", "Compliance pack (SOC2 report + subprocessor list)", "Benchmark script (Miguel)"

Final Recap (verbatim from call):
- Sunrise plans to increase reserved capacity to ~12 GPUs in us-west for Q3 and add eu-west with ~4 GPUs.
- Sunrise is evaluating a 12-month contract extension with committed reserved units; expected discount ~18-22% on unit pricing.
- Security: SOC2, SAML/SSO, KMS/HSM integration supported; legal wants subprocessor list and data residency details.
- Action items: pricing sheet, perf/inst config, benchmark script + sandbox run, contract amendment draft, traffic forecast.

Next meeting: tentative follow-up week of 2026-05-11 to review perf and contract draft.
